extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent agents/attorneys, and patent examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory rules and procedural standards under 35 U.S.C. (selected sections) governing inventorship, who may file, priority/benefit of earlier filing dates (foreign, provisional, domestic), divisional applications, confidentiality/publication, third-party pre‑issuance submissions, micro entity status, examination, rejection/reexamination, prosecution timing, and appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventors (35 U.S.C. 116)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an invention is made by two or more persons jointly, they shall apply for patent jointly and each make the required oath, except as otherwise provided in this title. Inventors may apply for a patent jointly even though (1) they did not physically work together or at the same time, (2) each did not make the same type or amount of contribution, or (3) each did not make a contribution to the subject matter of every claim of the patent. If a joint inventor refuses to join in an application for patent or cannot be found or reached after diligent effort, the application may be made by the other inventor on behalf of himself and the omitted inventor. Whenever through error a person is named as the inventor, or an inventor is not named, and such error arose without deceptive intention, the Director may permit amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key points: joint inventorship does not require equal contribution or contemporaneous work; provisions allow filing on behalf of an omitted or uncooperative inventor upon proof; errors in naming may be corrected if not deceptive. (Editor notes mark applicability changes for proceedings commenced on/after Sept. 16, 2012.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Death or incapacity of inventor (35 U.S.C. 117)
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal representatives of deceased inventors and of those under legal incapacity may make application for patent upon compliance with the requirements and on the same terms and conditions applicable to the inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits heirs or legal representatives to act as applicants under the same procedural requirements as the inventor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing by other than inventor (35 U.S.C. 118)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person to whom the inventor has assigned or is under an obligation to assign the invention may make an application for patent. A person who otherwise shows sufficient proprietary interest may make an application on behalf of and as agent for the inventor on proof of the pertinent facts and a showing that such action is appropriate to preserve the rights of the parties. If the Director grants a patent on such application, the patent shall be granted to the real party in interest and upon such notice to the inventor as the Director considers sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers filing by assignees, obligated assignees, agents with proprietary interest; requires proof and appropriate notice. Editor notes indicate different statutory applicability for pre‑AIA vs post‑AIA filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefit of earlier foreign filing; right of priority (35 U.S.C. 119)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application filed in the U.S. by a person who previously regularly filed an application for the same invention in a foreign country (that affords similar privileges or is a WTO member) shall have the same effect as if filed on the date of the foreign filing if the U.S. application is filed within 12 months from the earliest foreign filing date. The Director may by regulation permit an additional 2 months if the delay was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantial details and requirements: (b) a timely claim for priority identifying the foreign application number, authority/country, and filing date must be filed when required by the Director; failure to timely claim may be considered a waiver, but the Director may accept unintentionally delayed claims and may require a certified copy, translation, and other information; (c) right may be based on a subsequent foreign application under conditions (earlier application withdrawn/abandoned and not laid open); (d) inventors' certificates treated like patent applications for priority; (e) provisions for provisional applications (12‑month benefit to nonprovisional if filed within 12 months, must contain specific reference to provisional; Director may permit 2‑month unintentional delay; provisional reliance limited if required fee unpaid; timing rules for weekend/holiday falling on 12‑month day); (f) plant breeder rights in WTO/UPOV countries treated similarly; (g) definitions (WTO member, UPOV). Also includes amendment and certification requirements and potential fees (section 41(a)(7)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic benefit of earlier filing date (35 U.S.C. 120)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for patent in the U.S. for an invention disclosed as provided by section 112(a) in a previously filed U.S. application (or as provided by section 363/385) that names an inventor in the earlier application shall have the same effect as though filed on the date of the prior application if filed before patenting, abandonment, or termination of proceedings on the first application and if it contains or is amended to contain a specific reference to the earlier filed application. No application is entitled to the benefit unless the amendment containing the specific reference is submitted at such time during pendency as required by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director may deem failure to submit the required amendment a waiver and may establish procedures (including fees) to accept unintentionally delayed submissions. (Editor notes as to AIA applicability and pre‑AIA versions.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional applications (35 U.S.C. 121)
rubrics_metrics.description: If two or more independent and distinct inventions are claimed in one application, the Director may require restriction to one invention. If the other invention is the subject of a divisional application complying with section 120 it shall be entitled to the benefit of the filing date of the original application. A patent issuing on an application subject to a restriction requirement, or on an application filed as a result of such requirement, shall not be used as a reference against a divisional or the original application if the divisional is filed before issuance of the patent on the other application. The validity of a patent shall not be questioned for failure of the Director to require restriction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains restriction/divisional practice and protection from using parent/divisional patents as prior art against each other when divisional filed before issuance; Director may dispense with inventor signature on a divisional if it is directed solely to subject matter described and claimed in the original application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and publication of applications (35 U.S.C. 122)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications shall be kept in confidence by the Office except as provided in subsection (b). Subject to paragraph (2), each application shall be published promptly after 18 months from the earliest filing date for which a benefit is sought; applicant may request earlier publication. No information concerning published patent applications shall be made available to the public except as the Director determines; Director's determination to release or not to release is final and nonreviewable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions to publication: (b)(2)(A) application no longer pending; subject to secrecy order under section 181; a provisional application; or a design patent application. Nonpublication request (b)(2)(B)(i): applicant can request nonpublication upon filing certifying that no corresponding foreign/ international application that requires 18‑month publication will be filed; rescission allowed; if applicant later files abroad, they must notify Director within 45 days or application is regarded as abandoned. Redacted publication allowed when applicant has foreign filings with narrower descriptions; Director may publish redacted copy and section 154(d) doesn't apply to claims not enabled by redacted description. (d) National security: no publication if detrimental; Director to maintain secrecy under chapter 17.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑issuance third‑party submissions (35 U.S.C. 122(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any third party may submit for consideration any patent, published patent application, or other printed publication of potential relevance to the examination of the application, if such submission is made in writing before the earlier of (A) the date a notice of allowance is given or mailed, or (B) the later of (i) 6 months after the application is first published by the Office, or (ii) the date of the first rejection under section 132 of any claim by the examiner during examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission requirements (122(e)(2)): must (A) set forth a concise description of the asserted relevance of each submitted document; (B) be accompanied by such fee as the Director may prescribe; and (C) include a statement by the person making the submission affirming compliance with the section. Director may establish procedures and fees; timing rules are strict. (Also related text on protest and pre‑issuance opposition procedures.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Micro entity status and requirements (35 U.S.C. 123)
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of this title, 'micro entity' means an applicant who certifies that the applicant: (1) qualifies as a small entity under regulations; (2) has not been named as an inventor on more than 4 previously filed patent applications (with specified exceptions); (3) in the calendar year preceding fee payment had gross income not exceeding 3 times the median household income for that year; and (4) has not assigned, granted, or conveyed (and is not under an obligation to do so) a license or other ownership interest in the application to an entity whose gross income in the preceding calendar year exceeded 3 times the median household income.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsections cover: (b) applications resulting from prior employment excluded from counting prior applications if inventor assigned all rights as result of prior employment; (c) foreign currency exchange rate rules for income threshold; (d) inclusion of institutions of higher education under specified conditions; (e) Director's authority to impose additional income/filing limits with notice to congressional committees; (f) penalty for false certifications: an entity falsely certifying is subject to a fine determined by the Director of not less than 3 times the amount the entity failed to pay as a result of the false certification. (Added/ amended statutory history noted.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of application (35 U.S.C. 131)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall cause an examination to be made of the application and the alleged new invention; and if on such examination it appears that the applicant is entitled to a patent under the law, the Director shall issue a patent therefor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes the statutory duty to examine applications and issue patents when entitlement is found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of rejection; reexamination; continued examination (35 U.S.C. 132)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever, on examination, any claim is rejected, or any objection or requirement made, the Director shall notify the applicant stating the reasons for such rejection, or objection or requirement, together with such information and references as may be useful in judging the propriety of continuing prosecution; and if after receiving such notice the applicant persists in his claim for a patent, with or without amendment, the application shall be reexamined. No amendment shall introduce new matter into the disclosure of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director must prescribe regulations to provide for continued examination at the request of the applicant; Director may establish fees for continued examination and shall provide a 50% reduction in such fees for qualifying small entities. Emphasizes requirement to state reasons and supply references useful to applicant; prohibition on introduction of new matter in amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for prosecuting application; abandonment (35 U.S.C. 133)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon failure of the applicant to prosecute the application within six months after any action therein, of which notice has been given or mailed to the applicant, or within such shorter time, not less than thirty days, as fixed by the Director in such action, the application shall be regarded as abandoned by the parties thereto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default prosecution period is six months after Office action notice unless a shorter but not less than 30‑day period is fixed; failure to act within the period results in abandonment. (Statutory amendments and effective dates noted elsewhere.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board / Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences (35 U.S.C. 134)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant for a patent, any of whose claims has been twice rejected, may appeal from the decision of the primary examiner to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board, having once paid the fee for such appeal. A patent owner in a reexamination may appeal from the final rejection of any claim by the primary examiner to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board, having once paid the fee for such appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute contains transitional and pre‑AIA variants (editor notes) governing which board/process applies depending on filing/proceeding dates. Basic rule: after two rejections an applicant may appeal, and patent owners in reexam may appeal final rejections, subject to payment of the appeal fee.
